info.title: maison.table
info.description:
Table management for hotel restaurants. The minimum inventory record an agent needs to answer "is there a seat", hold it, and explain itself when the answer is no. Every refusal names a typed binding_constraint. Quote and commit are separate, joined by an availability token and a TTL-bounded hold.

**Tenancy** — no request ever carries a clientId field: the client comes from the credential. (Naming standard: the tenant is always called **client** — never org or tenant; a *property* is a building/location within a client, so one client can run several restaurants.) User JWTs carry the `client` claim (the client picked in the portal's client switcher; null = all clients, which this app resolves only when it serves exactly one client). Machine credentials (mk_ API keys, OAuth clients) are scoped to exactly ONE client in the portal — one key never serves multiple clients; give each client its own credential. Within the resolved client, `propertyId` selects the restaurant (from listProperties) and every query is additionally filtered server-side by the credential's client — a propertyId from another client returns nothing, never leaks.

**Times** — two kinds of timestamp live in this document, and they are not interchangeable. A *booking* time (`startsAt`, `endsAt`, an alternative slot, an assignment) is the property's own wall clock carried as Z: "19:30 at the restaurant" is `19:30:00Z` whatever the restaurant's real offset. Append `Z` to the operator's typed time and render by slicing the string — never convert, and never send a real UTC offset; a non-zero offset is refused (400), because this system has no zone to convert it into and the hour booked would not be the hour checked. A *record* time (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `bookedAt`, `cancelledAt`, `occurredAt`, a hold's or quote's `expiresAt`) is an ordinary instant in true UTC — those you may convert freely.

**Paging** — a list is a page, and the page says so. `searchReservations` returns a JSON array capped at `limit` (200 by default, 1000 at most) with the page's facts in the response headers: `X-Total-Count` is how many rows match in the database, `X-Has-More` is `true` when rows lie past this page, and `X-Page-Limit` / `X-Page-Offset` are the window you were served. A property's book runs to hundreds of live bookings, so **"I did not see it" is not "it does not exist" while `X-Has-More` is true**: narrow the search with `date`, or walk the book with `offset` in steps of `limit` until the header reads false.

bearerAuth.description: Portal-issued JWT (user or OAuth machine token, validated against the portal JWKS) or a portal API key (mk_…).

BindingConstraint.description: Typed refusal reason — why the answer is no (§4.4).

RefusalDetail.description: The numbers behind the refusal, keyed by bindingConstraint — closed_no_season: { date } · closed_exception: { startsOn, endsOn } · outside_service_hours: { date, time, dayOfWeek (0=Mon) } · past_cutoff: { cutoff } · buyout_blocked: { party?, covers? } · closed_online: { startsOn, endsOn } · sold_out_pool: { pool, remaining, capacity } · pacing_saturated: { windowStart, windowMinutes, currentCount, maxUnits } or, for the online sub-ceiling, { windowStart, windowMinutes, currentCount, maxUnitsOnline, deskCanOverride: true } · no_asset_fit: { partySize, largestFree?, freeTableCount? } or { reason: "A table fits but is not bookable online", partySize } · unreachable: { error }. deactivateTable adds no_asset_fit: { reason: "planned_seatings", tableId, tableName, count, seatings[] }; deactivateArea adds no_asset_fit: { reason: "area_has_active_tables", areaId, areaName, count, tables[] }; createTable and updateTable add no_asset_fit: { reason: "area_retired", areaId, areaName } — the room the table was to go in has been retired, which no new Idempotency-Key resolves.

startsAt.description: Property wall-clock stored as Z ("19:15 at the restaurant" is 19:15Z) — render by slicing, never by converting.

endsAt.description: startsAt plus the turn the slot was evaluated over.

vacancies.description: Covers left in the tightest pool at that slot, when pools are declared.

Alternatives.description: Nearest slots on the same date that pass the full check for this party, channel and product, nearest-first (a tie goes to the earlier slot). Bounded to the operating window of the service the refused request was evaluated against — a fixed seating declared for 19:00 only offers nothing, never the à la carte times beside it; outside service hours, the day's services are the window. Present only for refusals another time of day can resolve — sold_out_pool, sold_out_product, pacing_saturated, no_asset_fit, outside_service_hours, past_cutoff. Absent (never guessed) when the whole day binds: closed_no_season, closed_exception, closed_online, buyout_blocked, unreachable.

time.description: HH:MM on the property's wall clock

serviceId.description: The service whose declared slot this is — a fixed seating and an à la carte service can both declare 19:00. Absent when a single startTime was checked directly.

vacancies.description: Covers left in the tightest pool, when pools are declared. Present on available slots.

status.description: Where the booking stands. The first eight are the stored states (the reservation_status enum). **arrived and seated are derived**: searchReservations reads the booking's fulfillment as it loads the book and layers the arrival state on top (due_in → arrived, in_progress → seated), so a row returned by searchReservations can carry either — accept them. No reservation row ever holds them, which is why they cannot be used as a `status` filter; a terminal state on the reservation itself (cancelled, no_show, completed) always wins over the fulfillment. getReservation returns the stored state only. **None of the three terminal states is final**: `reinstateReservation` returns a cancelled, no-show or completed booking to a live state — taking no table and shown on none (`assignedTable` comes back null), which is what makes it safe to offer.

bookedAt.description: True instant — when the booking was taken, not the hour it is for

cancelledAt.description: True instant — when it was cancelled. Null while the booking stands; the row is never deleted (rule 7), and reinstateReservation clears this back to null along with the cancellation reason, so a booking that is back on the book never still says when it was cancelled

lines.description: The booked slots. Each line carries `startsAt`/`endsAt` as property wall-clock-as-Z (see **Times**), its covers (adults, children) and its serviceId.

assignedTable.description: The table the booking's first line is on, by name — two joined tables read "T12 + T13" — and null when it is on none. **Present on searchReservations rows only**: getReservation and every write verb answer with the reservation row, which has no such field. It reports every assignment that is not `superseded`, so last night's finished booking still shows the table its party actually sat at, while a table the booking moved away from, was cancelled off or never turned up for shows nothing — listing one of those would put a party on two tables at once. A reinstated booking reports null: the reversal supersedes every row that showed it on a table (see reinstateReservation). It is a display of the assignment record, not a claim on inventory — what a table's occupancy is decided by is the availability check.

overriddenConstraints.description: Limits an operator pushed through when booking or modifying. Null when none. Never set for online channels or machine credentials.

Season.description: A published Season is the only thing that makes dates bookable (closed by default). Archiving is a state change, never a delete.

timezone.description: IANA zone; defaults to the property's

updatedAt.description: True instant (timestamptz) — bumped on every attributed write

Service.description: A Service inside a Season declares the bookable window; its slots are generated from firstBookingTime to lastBookingTime every slotIntervalMinutes. Removing one sets status inactive — never a delete.

appliesDays.description: Seven flags, Monday first: 1 = the service runs that weekday

lastBookingTime.description: HH:MM:SS wall clock — the last slot start

turnOverrides.description: Turn time by party-size band, overriding defaultTurnMinutes

updatedAt.description: True instant (timestamptz) — bumped on every attributed write

Area.description: A room or zone of a property; a table declares which one it is in. Retiring an area sets status inactive and takes it out of listAreas and every picker — never a delete, so the bookings that sat in it still resolve which room that was.

updatedAt.description: True instant (timestamptz) — bumped on every attributed write

Table.description: A physical asset (canonical name: physical_asset). Joins are derived from joinableWith — never enumerated. Deactivating sets status inactive and removes it from the sellable set; history and past seatings stay.

joinableWith.description: Adjacent asset ids — declared once, combinations derived

onlineBookable.description: Channel state — a table can be open to the desk and closed online

updatedAt.description: True instant (timestamptz) — bumped on every attributed write

entityType.description: Canonical XOS entity name — a table is a physical_asset. fulfillment events are logged against the reservation's id, so a reservation's history carries its arrival flow.

eventType.description: Every value the services emit today. A service change is logged twice: on the service and on its season (season.service_*), so the season's history reads on its own.

actorId.description: The principal that acted; null for system

actorName.description: Resolved: the name stamped in the payload at write time, else the principal's display name, else actorType

payload.description: What changed — e.g. { changes } on *.updated, { name, startsOn, endsOn, timezone } on season.created, { actorName } on fulfillment.*, { from, to, unseated: true, warnings? } on reservation.reinstated (`unseated` is the safety property on the record: the booking came back without a table). Never personal data on declaration entities.

correlationId.description: Ties the events of one operation together — the caller's x-correlation-id, or one minted per request

updatedAt.description: True instant (timestamptz) — bumped on every attributed write

Error.description: Every non-2xx body. `error` is the operator-readable message; when a §4.4 constraint binds, `bindingConstraint` names it and `detail` carries the numbers; `alternatives` is present only when another time of day could resolve the refusal.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional but recommended, and honoured by EVERY /config write. The key names one operation: send it again for the same operation on the same record and the first write's result comes back, unchanged and unlogged — which is what makes a retry after a lost answer safe. Reusing it for a different operation, or for the same operation on a different record, is a client error and is refused (409) rather than answered with the first record. A blank key, or one longer than 255 characters, is refused (400) instead of silently ignored: a key that is dropped would promise a guarantee that is not there. Omit it entirely and the write is deduped against nothing — one write per request.

OptionalIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
OptionalIdempotencyKey.description: Optional but recommended. The key names one operation: send it again for the same operation on the same booking and the first write's result stands — nothing is written twice and nothing is logged twice — which is what makes a retry after a lost answer safe. These three operations are idempotent by state as well (the booking is already cancelled, already in that arrival state, already live), so a keyless caller is not left unprotected; the key closes the concurrent-retry race that state alone cannot. A blank key, or one longer than 255 characters, is refused (400) rather than silently ignored: a dropped key would promise a guarantee that is not there.

CorrelationId.name: x-correlation-id
CorrelationId.description: Ties every event of this call together in event_logs (correlationId). Kept when sent, minted when absent; a non-UUID value is refused (400), never silently replaced.

post.summary: Check availability across a day — every slot, with a typed refusal when the answer is no

startTime.description: HH:MM on the property's wall clock. Alone it checks that one slot; with endTime it bounds the range.

endTime.description: HH:MM on the property's wall clock — the last slot start considered.

sourceChannel.description: The channel this booking will be made on — send the one you will pass to createReservation. `web` and `ota` are evaluated as online (close_online, the online pacing sub-ceiling and every table with online_bookable = false all apply); the rest are the desk. Omitted means the desk, unless the credential is a machine.

isOnline.description: Escape hatch for a caller that has already resolved the channel itself. `true` forces the online rules; it never turns them off — an online sourceChannel or a machine credential still wins. A machine credential (mk_ key, OAuth client) is always evaluated as online whatever it sends (T7).

200.description: Per-slot availability, each slot evaluated against the service that declared it (serviceId); unavailable slots carry bindingConstraint, detail and, where another time could work, the nearest slots in that service's window that pass the same check. Business refusals are answers, not errors — always 200 with a typed reason (Google convention). `startTime` alone checks that single slot; with `endTime` it bounds the range.

400.description: Missing propertyId, date or partySize

503.description: The availability engine could not answer (bindingConstraint: unreachable, detail: { error }) — hand to phone. Never a 200 with a guess.

post.summary: Quote one slot — returns an opaque availability token (TTL-bounded) to hold or book against

time.description: HH:MM on the property's wall clock

sourceChannel.description: The channel this booking will be made on — send the one you will pass to createReservation. `web` and `ota` are evaluated as online (close_online, the online pacing sub-ceiling and every table with online_bookable = false all apply); the rest are the desk. Omitted means the desk, unless the credential is a machine.

isOnline.description: Escape hatch for a caller that has already resolved the channel itself. `true` forces the online rules; it never turns them off — an online sourceChannel or a machine credential still wins. A machine credential (mk_ key, OAuth client) is always evaluated as online whatever it sends (T7).

200.description: The quote — persisted either way. `available: true` carries the availabilityId to hold or book against within its TTL; a refusal is still 200 with `available: false`, the bindingConstraint, its detail and the nearest alternatives in the same service's window (rule 5).

availabilityId.description: Opaque token joining quote to commit

serviceId.description: The service this quote priced — pass through to hold/createReservation. Absent only on a refusal at a time no service covers

sellableProductId.description: Deprecated alias of serviceId — same value, kept for pre-rename clients

vacancies.description: Covers left in the tightest pool, when pools are declared

400.description: Missing propertyId, date, time or partySize

default.description: Any typed service error keeps its status; where a constraint binds the body carries bindingConstraint, detail and alternatives. Engine failures are 500 with a generic message — never a guess.

post.summary: Hold inventory against a quote — decrements pools for its TTL; never oversells

schema.description: serviceId (or its deprecated alias sellableProductId) is required alongside these — either name satisfies it. The value is the quote's, and the hold claims what the QUOTE priced: the service is read from the quote row server-side.

400.description: Missing Idempotency-Key header or a required field

409.description: Quote expired / inventory gone / hold cap reached (MAX_HOLDS_PER_API_KEY, MAX_HOLDS_PER_CLIENT) — message only; hold refusals carry no bindingConstraint today

delete.summary: Release a hold before it expires

500.description: Hold not found, not active, or already expired

post.summary: Extend a hold's TTL (bounded by HOLD_EXTEND_MAX_SECONDS)

500.description: Hold not found, not active, or already expired

post.summary: Commit a reservation — from a hold, or directly with an in-transaction availability re-check

serviceId.description: Optional — server resolves the hold's service, else the ordinary service covering the time

startsAt.description: The property's own wall clock, sent and stored as Z: "19:30 at the restaurant" is 2026-08-23T19:30:00Z, whatever the restaurant's real offset. Append Z to the operator's typed time — never convert, and never send a browser or property offset. Accepted: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, with optional seconds and optional fractional seconds, bare or with a trailing Z (a zero offset, +00:00, is the same instant). Refused with 400: any non-zero UTC offset — this system has no zone to convert one into, so honouring it would book an hour nobody asked for — and any date-time that is not real (2026-02-31, 24:00). Seconds are dropped: the check runs at minute granularity, so the instant stored is the instant evaluated.

sourceChannel.description: How this booking reached the restaurant, recorded on the reservation. It also decides the channel the availability re-check runs on — `web` and `ota` are evaluated as online, and a machine credential always is (T7) — so quote with the same channel you commit with.

override.description: Push the booking through a rate/fit limit the evaluator named: pacing_saturated, no_asset_fit. Honoured only for a human operator on a non-online channel; ignored for web/ota and for machine credentials (the agent). Recorded on the reservation (overriddenConstraints) and in its event. Capacity, closures and buyouts can never be overridden.

409.description: Not available — refusal named by bindingConstraint

get.summary: Search the book — by date, status, party size. Cancelled bookings are excluded unless asked for; the answer is one page and the headers say whether more remain

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The property's calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD), matched against each line's wall-clock start.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Exactly one STORED status, from the list. An explicit status always wins: `status=cancelled` returns the cancellations whether or not includeCancelled is set, and no other status is affected by it. Anything outside the list is refused (400), never answered with an empty array — including `arrived` and `seated`, which this API emits on rows but cannot search on: they are read off the fulfillment at load time and no reservation row holds them (see Reservation.status). To work the floor, read the day (`date=YYYY-MM-DD`) and take the rows whose `status` is arrived or seated.

parameters.name: partySize
parameters.description: A floor, not an exact match: keeps reservations with a line of at least this many covers (adults + children). Applied in the query, so it narrows the book before the cap — never a thinned page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The cap on rows returned, applied after every filter. Defaults to 200, maximum 1000; anything else (0, a fraction, nonsense) is refused with a 400 naming the range rather than coerced. The rows are the newest seatings first, so the cap eats the far past — and `X-Total-Count` / `X-Has-More` on the response say whether it bit.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip in the ordered book — the way past the cap. The order is total (seating time descending, ties by id), so a book is walked deterministically: offset 0, then `limit`, then `2 × limit`, until `X-Has-More` reads false. Refused with a 400 if it is not a whole number of rows, 0 or more.

parameters.name: includeCancelled
parameters.description: Opt in to cancelled bookings. Default false: with no explicit `status`, the book is the bookings that are still on — a cancelled party is not coming, and leaving them in would seat a cancelled guest on the floor. Send `true` (or `1`) for the full record: guest history, an audit view, the reservation an operator opened deliberately. Any other value, including absent, is false. Ignored when `status` is given.

200.description: One page of matching reservations, newest seating first. Cancelled ones appear only when `includeCancelled=true` or `status=cancelled`; the default answer is the live book. **The body is a page, not the book**: the array holds at most `limit` rows and the headers say how much there is. Never conclude "there is no such booking" from an empty search while `X-Has-More` is true — narrow it with `date`, or walk it with `offset`.

X-Total-Count.description: Reservations matching the filters in the database, before the cap.

X-Has-More.description: `true` when matching rows lie past this page: ask again from `offset + limit`.

X-Page-Limit.description: The cap that was applied to this page.

X-Page-Offset.description: Where this page starts in the ordered book.

400.description: Missing propertyId; a status that is not one of the stored reservation states (arrived and seated are derived — see the `status` parameter); or a limit/offset that is not a whole number in range

get.summary: One reservation with lines and guest

404.description: Not found

patch.summary: Modify date/time, party, table, guest details or notes. Availability is re-checked whenever what the booking occupies could have moved — the slot, the party, or a product whose service declares a different turn; a party that no longer fits its table saves with a warning (table_too_small / no_asset_fit) — pool and pacing refusals still fail closed with a named constraint.

startsAt.description: The property's own wall clock, sent and stored as Z: "19:30 at the restaurant" is 2026-08-23T19:30:00Z, whatever the restaurant's real offset. Append Z to the operator's typed time — never convert, and never send a browser or property offset. Accepted: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, with optional seconds and optional fractional seconds, bare or with a trailing Z (a zero offset, +00:00, is the same instant). Refused with 400: any non-zero UTC offset — this system has no zone to convert one into, so honouring it would book an hour nobody asked for — and any date-time that is not real (2026-02-31, 24:00). Seconds are dropped: the check runs at minute granularity, so the instant stored is the instant evaluated.

tableId.description: A physical asset of the same property

override.description: Push the booking through a rate/fit limit the evaluator named: pacing_saturated, no_asset_fit. Honoured only for a human operator on a non-online channel; ignored for web/ota and for machine credentials (the agent). Recorded on the reservation (overriddenConstraints) and in its event. Capacity, closures and buyouts can never be overridden.

200.description: Modified. `warnings` lists constraints that were noted but did not block the save.

404.description: Reservation or table not found at this property

409.description: New slot not available — `bindingConstraint` names why

post.summary: Cancel — a state change, never a delete; inventory is returned
post.description: The booking, its lines and its fulfillment go to `cancelled`, the tables it held are released and the covers go back to the pools. Idempotent: an already-cancelled booking is returned untouched. Reversible — a cancellation taken by mistake, or a guest who calls back, is put back on the book with `reinstateReservation`, which returns it to a live state WITHOUT a table.

400.description: Missing reason, or a blank or oversized Idempotency-Key

404.description: Reservation not found in this client

post.summary: Arrival flow the floor runs from a phone: arrived → seated → completed, or no_show
post.description:
Every one of the four is logged as `fulfillment.<status>` in the booking's history. `arrived` and `seated` live on the fulfillment and leave the reservation itself `confirmed` — they are layered onto the row when searchReservations loads the book. `no_show` and `completed` are terminal: they land on the reservation row too and release its tables. Setting the state a booking is already in adds nothing to its history.

This endpoint only ever moves a booking FORWARD or hands a table back; it never puts a party back onto a table, because it has neither the clash check nor the availability re-check that takes one (rules 5 and 8). So a booking that has ENDED — cancelled, no-show or completed — is refused `arrived` and `seated` here (409). The way back is `reinstateReservation`: it returns the booking to a live state with no table, and `modifyReservation` with a `tableId` then places it through the path that checks.

200.description: Status set — logged as fulfillment.<status> in the reservation's history

400.description: Missing or invalid status, or a blank or oversized Idempotency-Key

404.description: Reservation not found in this client

409.description: The booking has ended and this status would put it back on a table: `arrived` or `seated` on a cancelled, no-show or completed booking. Reinstate it first (`reinstateReservation`), then place it with `modifyReservation`. `no_show` and `completed` are accepted on an ended booking — they take nothing.

post.summary: Confirm an inquiry — the sale, checked in full at the inquiry's own time and party
post.description: An inquiry is a guest asking, recorded (an imported or emailed request the book could not take as-is — outside service hours, no season, a saturated window). It consumes nothing until confirmed. Confirming is a SALE: the full availability check under the day's lock, never reinstate's warn-and-proceed. An operator may push through the overridable constraints (pacing, fit) with an attributed override, exactly as on create; walls refuse with the constraint named and the inquiry stands.

409.description: Refused — bindingConstraint names the wall; alternatives where a time shift could work

post.summary: Put an ended booking back on the book — the reversal of cancelled, no_show, completed. It returns `confirmed` and WITHOUT a table.
post.description:
Every end a booking comes to is reversible: a no-show who walks in after all, a party marked finished while it is still sitting, a mis-tapped cancel. Reinstating returns the booking to `confirmed` — on the book, searchable, modifiable — and with it the lines, the fulfillment (`pre_arrival`, check-out cleared) and, for a cancellation, the covers it had given back. `cancelledAt` and the cancellation reason are cleared: a booking that is back on must not still say when it was cancelled.

**It never TAKES a table, and it comes back on none.** The reversal commits no inventory, and it leaves no row saying otherwise: every assignment that still shows the booking on a table is superseded on the way — the `planned` and `active` rows the room counts for occupancy, AND the `completed` row a closed-out seating leaves behind, which takes no table but does put the booking on one in the book. So a reinstated booking reports `assignedTable: null` in `searchReservations` and occupies nothing; the table it had was handed back when it ended and may well have been re-sold since, which is why the reversal supersedes that row rather than reviving it. Put the party on a table with `modifyReservation` (`tableId`), which is the one path that runs the clash check and the availability re-check. That is what makes the reversal safe to offer at all, and why reinstating can never seat two parties on one table — in the room's arithmetic or on the operator's screen.

**The covers do come back, and that is not refused.** A live booking consumes its pools and its pacing window again, which is correct — the party really is coming — and it can put the night over its cap, because the book was free to re-sell those covers while this booking was off it. A reinstatement is a CORRECTION, not a sale: the overage is reported in `warnings` and never blocks the reversal, since refusing would leave the book asserting something false about a party at the door with no way to fix it.

Idempotent by state and by key (rule 6): a booking that is already live is returned untouched with no warnings and nothing logged.

This API notifies nobody — nothing here sends an email or an SMS. The guest may already have been told a cancelled table was gone, so whoever reinstates owns that conversation.

200.description: Reinstated (reservation.reinstated) — `status` is `confirmed`, `cancelledAt` is null, and the booking is on NO table: this body is the reservation row, which carries no table field, and a `searchReservations` afterwards reports `assignedTable: null` for it, because the reversal superseded every assignment row that still showed it on one (the `completed` row of a closed-out seating included). `warnings` says what the room looks like now; it is advice, not a refusal, and an empty array means the covers fit. Never quote a table to the guest from this response — assign one with modifyReservation first.

warnings.description: What the reinstatement had to say about the room, evaluated with this booking's own covers excluded. Only constraints about the INVENTORY are reported: a season, closure or service-hours refusal answers "may this slot be sold", and the slot was already sold once — undoing last month's mis-tapped completion would otherwise always come back carrying `closed_no_season`, which is noise an operator learns to ignore.

message.example: The room is full at 19:30; these 4 covers take it over. The covers were re-sold while the booking was off the book.

400.description: A blank or oversized Idempotency-Key

404.description: Reservation not found in this client

409.description: Refused by the booking's STATE, not by the room — no bindingConstraint is named, because no constraint bound. Either the booking has no end to reverse (only cancelled, no_show, completed do: an `inquiry` or a `quoted` never took inventory and never ended, so turning one into a confirmed booking is a SALE and goes through createReservation, which checks) — or the Idempotency-Key was already used for a different operation, or for this one on a different booking.

500.description: A fault, not a refusal. `error` is always the fixed string "Internal server error" — only sentences the service wrote deliberately reach a caller, and a failed statement carries its own SQL and parameter values. The detail is in the operator log. Do not show a 500 body to a user or branch on its text; the write may or may not have landed, so retry it under the SAME Idempotency-Key and the answer will be the first attempt's result if it did.

get.summary: The client's properties — the entry point; everything else is keyed by propertyId

200.description: Active properties of the credential's client

patch.summary: Edit a property's name, timezone, currency or address — attributed (property.updated)
patch.description: Attributed and idempotent (rule 6). The timezone is what "19:00 at the restaurant" is measured against for every future booking (see **Times**), so the edit is traceable to a principal and a retry under one Idempotency-Key replays the first write.

400.description: A body that is not a JSON object, a malformed field value (a non-integer where the contract says integer, a non-UUID id, an unresolvable IANA time zone, a currency that is not a three-letter ISO 4217 code), a missing required field, no changes provided, a blank or oversized Idempotency-Key, or a non-UUID x-correlation-id

404.description: Property not found in this client

409.description: Idempotency-Key was already used for a different operation, or for this operation on a different record
